FINDING_ID: C0029
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.8
DESCRIPTION: FIND — In `evaluate_fix()`, the target source file is copied to an isolated temporary directory (`tmpdir`) before executing static analysis tools and the `test_cmd`.
FOLLOW: Because the patched file is evaluated entirely out-of-tree, typecheckers (like Pyright/Mypy) fail to resolve internal workspace imports, generating massive false-positive type errors. Furthermore, the test command (`pytest bench/tests/`) fails instantly because the workspace structure and test paths do not exist in the empty temporary directory. Consequently, every proposed fix evaluates to `HARMFUL`, completely destroying the fix evaluation capability on the happy path.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Instead of copying the file to an isolated temp directory, modify the target file in-place, execute the tools with standard workspace paths (`cwd=None`), and guarantee restoration of the original file contents using a `try...finally` block. Remove the `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` isolation wrapping.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: C0030
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.6
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_apply_fix_to_source()` Strategy 2 calls `compile(fix, "<fix>", "exec")` and treats any valid Python snippet with >= 5 newlines as a complete whole-file replacement.
FOLLOW: If a model proposes a partial function rewrite (e.g., 6 lines of code) without using the exact search-replace format, Strategy 2 deletes the rest of the target file, replacing it with just those 6 lines. If `test_cmd` is not provided (meaning tests don't run to catch the deletion), this tiny valid script will often have zero lint/type errors compared to a full module, resulting in `total_net < 0`. The destructive replacement will falsely evaluate as `SAFE`, improperly verifying the finding and closing the bug while deleting the file.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Remove Strategy 2 entirely. Models must rely on explicit search-replace blocks (Strategy 1) or `Line N:` formats (Strategy 3), which securely bounds modifications without the risk of silent file deletion.
VERIFIED: TRUE
